body:
POST-MERGE AND POST-CLOSURE CLEANUP. Current procedure from Greg's standing direction via Advisor message19c59c2c, 2026-10-29T19:54:37Z, relayed by Engram::Fable message3f6c938a-13ca-43f1-9b70-cb783f29dd0f; also the earlier direction via Advisor message2d0b8be9-1be8-4a93-9220-06be6cd19a38. This adds no landing gate or commit/restart authority.

After a successful merge AND closure of the associated work, the Merger/lander automatically removes its worktree and unneeded build output as part of the ordinary completion process. Do not stop at writing REMOVE or wait for Greg to remind anyone. If another session closes the last task, it hands cleanup to the Merger/coordinator through the existing handoff route. Cleanup is an owned action; this procedure does not itself create a host timer or automatic wake.

RETAIN is allowed only for a concrete, recorded and STILL ACTIVE need, such as an indispensable open investigation or a shared root's remaining active work. Record the exact task/use, accountable owner and event ending retention; check that the reason still holds. Generic "may be useful", an expired use or an anonymous "later" is not a reason. The coordinator's regular sweep enforces removal when that need ends. Record actual landing, closure, REMOVE/RETAIN and completion of removal on the task for root, local branch, build output, logs and raw evidence.

Before removal, all runs must be terminal and their outcomes recovered/recorded; no pending notification or review may still depend on the root. Verify no active claim/process, frozen input still in use, unique dirty/unpushed work or unresolved citation by open work. Record any real safety blocker with owner, next action and release condition, and resolve it through the ordinary coordinator process. Age, directory name, released claim or process absence alone proves no disposability. Preserve durable decision facts in Engram notes/gates/seals.

If required evidence exists only in the retiring root, copy only that needed evidence and reproduction context to the main checkout's ignored .evidence directory; verify the copy, preserve original result/freeze bytes and update old-to-new paths on every known citing task before removal. Reference existing durable Git/tool records where sufficient, following the current minimal-evidence rule; no routine manifest/hash bundle, whole-target archive or copy of every closed task's artifacts. Unclear references remain a recorded retention blocker. The existing historical cleanup task owns the full citation census for legacy/uninventoried roots; do not add that census to every new landing.

Remove the clean completed worktree through git worktree remove without --force. Delete a stale local branch only when proven integrated into published main/master, with no unique unpushed commits and no other worktree using it; use git branch -d, never -D. Preserve main/master, remote refs, active roots and needed frozen inputs. Do not discard dirty work or create replacement task roots to evade retention.

Before any recursive deletion, resolve and validate absolute paths inside the intended repository, check junctions/symlinks and shared build-directory use, and never delete through an unchecked variable or broad git clean. Record exact removals and measured reclaimed space, attributing only this cleanup's own changes.

The agent closing the last task served by a retained .logs/.evidence file removes it, or the coordinator's sweep does, once its recorded need ends. Preserve every artifact still needed by open work. A blocker remains tracked with its recovery owner and release condition; it does not turn into indefinite retention. No new review, evaluation, full gate or approval round is introduced for this post-completion action.
